newsitem.title: UK: Australia looks to Asia, but keeps foot in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Australia looks to Asia, but keeps foot in Europe.

text.p: Australia said on Wednesday that closer links with the burgeoning Asia Pacific region were its highest priority but that it would not turn its back on old friends in Europe.

In a speech in London outlining Australia's foreign policy priorities, Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said East Asia was moving forward "at a pace and with a force that is unparalleled in recent history".

"Australia's highest foreign policy is closer engagement with Asia. But an Asia first priority does not mean Asia only," Downer told the Royal Institute of International Affairs during an official visit to Britain.
"Just as Australia would urge Europe not to be narrowly Euro-centric, the Australian government will not make the mistake of being exclusively concerned with our immediate region," he added.

Downer said that eight of Australia's top 10 trading partners were located in the Asia Pacific region and that sustained growth in the region presented immense opportunities for both Australia and Europe.
He said Australia was keen to strengthen security cooperation with its Asia Pacific neighbours and was keen to involve China in these discussions.

"China needs to be involved and integrated into the emerging regional security community...I am convinced of the benefits of working co-operatively with it both bilaterally and in regional security processes," Downer said.
He said Australia wanted to enhance its already strong commercial relations with Europe and was keen for improved access, particularly in the agriculture and coal sectors.
Australian farmers had suffered badly from the European Union's Common Agricultural Policy and the trade deficit with the EU had doubled since 1990, he said.

He noted that Australia had already revitalised its relations with France following a row over French nuclear tests in the Pacific last year, and that Australia had established political-military links with Germany.
Earlier on Wednesday, Downer launched a bilateral trade and cultural promotion with its colonial ruler Britain, aimed at removing mutual stereotypes.

Urging Europe to work with Australia, he said that, in an increasingly integrated world, "the long-term stability and development of Asia Pacific will also have a progressively greater impact on Europe's prospects."
